findings.summary: runtime topology changes stalled SDL_GPU on a queue-wide idle and Dawn on a submitted-work callback before rebuilding, turning an ordinary mesh replacement into a whole-device synchronization point; both backends now rely on their resource-retirement guarantees and rematch live rows without blocking the queue

the SDL_GPU and Dawn topology rebuilds each restated the same forward two-pointer reconciliation, including the survivor, removal and append cases; one shared rematch_render_meshes helper now owns that invariant and moves surviving CPU rows instead of copying them

short-lived shader meshes uploaded every texture and sampler on every replacement even though the material handle and its texture set were unchanged; each backend now uploads that set once per live shader material and shares it across the material's mesh rows, cutting the 36-mesh churn probe from 35.1 ms to 15.9 ms average on SDL_GPU

the first shader geometry reuse cache retained every historical shape forever and made each exact-match scan grow with runtime duration; live mesh rows now reference-count stable cache entries and both backends retire zero-user geometry after make-before-break reconciliation

sharing shader-material textures initially introduced a second unbounded cache and a redundant owns_shader_textures flag; mesh rows now point at reference-counted entries, derive ownership from that pointer, and prune unused texture/sampler sets beside geometry

the exact shader-geometry comparison and material-cache lookup were copied between the two PALs; backend-neutral find_shared_shader_geometry and find_shared_shader_material_textures helpers keep the byte-comparison and handle-identity rules in one place while the concrete GPU resources remain backend-owned

Dawn released mesh resources only through an all-mesh loop, which made incremental topology teardown duplicate and risk reordering the bind-group-before-resource lifetime rule; release_mesh now owns the dependency order and both incremental removal and shutdown call it

the complete compiler and runtime diff was reviewed for duplicate lowering routes, redundant state, repeated hot-path work and ownership leaks; beyond the applied PAL findings, the remaining large data-lowering surface is feature-separated and directly covered by the new semantic compiler tests, so no additional high-confidence behavior-preserving merge was found
